1-01-01.01_课程介绍

您好，欢迎来到成功学课程。

我是理查德·谢尔。

我是沃顿商学院的一名资深教授。

我在这里已经工作了几十年。

我教授过很多门课程。

可能最广为人知的是我讲授的谈判与说服课程。

我也教授一门关于责任感的课程。

但是，我们将要一起学习的这门课程，是我教授并已经讲授了10年的课程，叫做“成功学文献”。

这实际上是一门探讨成功对于选修它的每一位学生究竟意味着什么的课程。

我们为你创建了这次在线学习体验，让你有机会加入我们，感受沃顿的氛围。

我会把这次课程，当作是你在我的办公时间来与我交流。

我们将探讨成功的各种不同要素，以及我们如何探索这些要素。

你会收到一些评估。

你会得到一些自我分析工具，它们将帮助你更深入地理解“成功”这个词对你的具体含义。

随着我们在整个课程中一起学习，我想你会发现，我会要求你挑战自我，去思考你真正持有的价值观，去思考那些影响了你、造就了今日之你、以及你之所以成为今日之你的家庭及各种影响，思考你是什么样的人，并希望能开始收集一些想法，关于你对“成功”这个词发自内心的、真诚的含义是什么，然后思考你个人如何才能以最适合自己的方式去实现它。

我们将通过一系列不同主题的课程来实现这一目标。

你会做一些关于价值观的功课。

你会做一些关于你个人能力和独特天赋的功课。

我们会深入探讨人们是如何取得成就的，以及成就的真正含义是什么。

我们还将深入探讨一个词，这个词在我们所处的文化中被频繁提及，但人们对它却知之甚少，这个词就是幸福。

然后，我会尽我所能，帮助你们将我们讨论过的内容，以一种你们可以运用的方式融入实际，采取行动，并在课程结束时开始制定具体的目标，这样你们就能开始对自己是谁、自己擅长什么、以及在人生的这个阶段应该朝着哪个方向前进，有了一些清晰的想法。

所以，我期待着与你们合作。

就像我说的，我们现在就在我的办公室里，这里将是我们进行整个课程的地方。

祝你们好运。

系好安全带。

我想你们会发现这门课既充满乐趣，又颇具挑战性。

我很期待。

英文原文

Hi,welcome to the Success Course.

My name is Richard Schell.

I'm a senior professor here at the Wharton School.

I've been here for decades.

I've taught many courses.

I'm probably best known for teaching courses on negotiation and persuasion.

I also teach a course on responsibility.

But the course we're going to work on together,the course we're going to do together,is a course that I teach and have taught for 10 years called The Literature of Success.

It's really a course on what success means for each individual student who takes it.

And we're creating this online experience for you to give you a chance to join us in a Wharton setting.

I'm going to be treating this as if you were coming to my office hours.

We're going to be talking about all the different elements of success and how we explore that.

You'll be getting assessments.

You'll be getting some sort of self-analysis tools that will help you understand a little bit more about what this big word success means to you.

And as we work together throughout this course,I think you're going to find that I'm going to be asking you to challenge yourself,to think about the values that you really hold,to think about the family of influences that have affected who you are and why you are,

what you are,and hopefully begin to gather some ideas about what your genuine,heartfelt meaning is for this word success,and then how individually you can go about achieving it in the best way for yourself.

We're going to do it through a series of classes on different topics.

You'll be doing some work on values.

You'll be doing some work on your capabilities and your unique talents.

We'll be looking deeply at how people achieve things,what achievement actually means.

Be looking in some depth at a word that the culture that we live in thinks a great deal of but doesn't really know much about,and that word is happiness.

And then I'm going to be doing what I can to help you to contextualize what we've talked about in a way that you can use,take action on,begin to formulate specific goals on by the end of the class so that you're beginning to have some clear ideas about who you are,what you do well,and the direction that you ought to take at this stage of your life.

So,I look forward to working with you.

We're sitting,as I said,in my office right here,and this is going to be the place where we handle the whole course.

So good luck.

Strap your seatbelt in.

I think you're going to find it a lot of fun and somewhat challenging.

So I look forward to it.

1-01-01.02_如何使用本课程

这门课会与商学院其他一些涉及分析技能或领导力方法的传统课程略有不同，因为这门课几乎完全是关于你自身的。

而对于你自身在课程将要探讨的问题上处于何种状态，你是最佳的评判者。

因此，学习并利用这门课程的一个方法就是，只需浏览一下不同课时和周的议题列表，然后点击一个看起来对你特别有意思或正合时宜的章节。

直接从中间开始学习。

然后尝试几个章节，开始感受我们将要讨论的材料的关联性，以及你如何能与之建立联系。

你可能想从头开始，按照我们编排的顺序学习一段时间，然后再跳到结尾部分。

你可能会发现，你对某些问题，比如有意义的工作或职业，有迫切的问题需要解答。

那么，请随意点击与这些问题相关的部分，你随时可以回来，在其它时间学习其余部分。

或者，最后一点，我们将这门课程设计成了一个从头到尾连贯、结构化的体验。

如果你只是从头开始，一直学到结尾，我想你会发现各个主题是相互衔接的，它们按一个有意义的顺序排列，彼此关联。

你会发觉，以传统方式学习这门课，就像你可能学习其他科目课程一样，会很有收获。

所以我希望你能随意地以最适合你的方式使用这门课程，因为正如我所说，这门课确实是关于你自身的。

英文原文

This course is going to be a little different than some of the other traditional business school courses that involve analytic skills or leadership methodologies because this course is almost entirely about you.

And you are the best judge of where you are with the questions that the course is going to address.

And so one way to take this course and use it would be to just simply look down the list of topics for the different sessions and weeks and click on one that looks like it's especially interesting or timely for you.

And just jump right in in the middle.

And then sample a few and begin to get a sense for the relevance of the material that we'll be talking through.

how you can connect to it.

You may want to start at the beginning and work for a while on the materials in the order that we put it,but then jump to the end.

You may find that you have some urgent questions about something like meaningful work or career.

And so go ahead and feel free to click on the parts that have relevance to that question and you can always come back and get to the other parts another time.

Or finally,we've made this course so that it's a coherent,structured experience from beginning to end.

And if you simply start at the beginning and work your way through to the end,I think you'll find that the topics build on one another,that they're related in a sequence that makes sense.

And you'll find it rewarding to take it in a traditional way,just the way you might take a course on another subject.

So I hope you'll feel free to use the course the way it works best for you because as I said,this course is really about you.

1-01-01.03_本课程的实用性

在我们学院的课程体系中，出现这样一门课程。

它有点新颖。

沃顿商学院的大多数课程都非常注重分析，非常注重工具的应用。

但在10年前我创建这门课程，审视整个课程体系时，我意识到，没有任何地方，无论是在沃顿，还是在宾夕法尼亚大学，能让学生花整整一个学期去思考那些最重要的问题，那些能帮助他们在未来人生中，当他们遇到不同的转折时刻时，比如下一步该做什么，当他们不得不搬到一个新城市时该做什么，当他们完成研究生学业时该做什么，

当他们改变职业时该做什么的问题。

我回顾了自己的人生，意识到多年来我积累了一些有用的经验，以及大量不同的知识基础，足以整合出这样一门课程。

所以，我想你们会发现，像我们将要共同学习的这样一门课程，会在以下几个方面对你们有所帮助。

我认为首先也是最重要的，我认为它会对你有所帮助。

我认为你将能够评估自己、你的价值观、你对成功含义的构想，从而更清晰地了解你的动机是什么。

如果你为人父母，或者担任他人的导师，你也可能会发现这门课程很有用，它可以帮助你阐述、引导那些同样面临这些问题的人，并在某种程度上充当他们的教练。

因此，我们将进行一系列不同的小型自我评估和练习，帮助你思考这个主题。

最终，我想你会发现，就像许多选修过这门课程的学生和高管一样，你会有豁然开朗的时刻，这应该能帮助你指引未来的道路。

英文原文

A course like this kind of comes up in our curriculum.

It's a little novel.

Most of the courses at Wharton are very analytic,they're very tools-based.

But looking over the curriculum 10 years ago when I created this course,I realized that there was nowhere,not at Wharton,not at the University of Pennsylvania,where a student could go and spend a whole semester thinking about the most important questions that would help them later in life as they encountered different transition moments,

what to do next,what to do when they had to move to a new city,what to do when they finished grad school,what to do when they changed careers.

And I looked back on my own life and realized that over the years I'd picked up some useful experiences and a lot of different knowledge bases to put together a course like this.

So I think you're going to find that a course like the course we're going to have together is going to be useful to you in one of several ways.

I think first and foremost,I think it'll help you.

I think you'll be able to assess yourself,your values,your images of what success means,come to a little more clarity on what's going on in your motivations.

If you're a parent or a mentor to others,you might also find this useful as a way of helping you articulate and guide and serve as a sort of coach for other people who are confronting these same questions.

So we're going to be doing a bunch of different little self-assessments,exercises to help you think about this subject.

And at the end of the day,I think you'll find that just like for many of the students and executives who've taken this,you'll have a few light bulbs go off that should help you guide your way to the future.

1-01-01.04_我教授本课程的原因

我教授这门课程，是因为在我自己的人生中，尤其是在我的教育经历中，我发现没有一个真正的地方可以让我去学习如何思考成功这个问题。

在我们的文化中，成功是一个意义重大且强有力的词。

每个人都想获得更多成功，但没有人真正确定它意味着什么。

大多数时候，当一切顺利时，你甚至不会去想它。

你只是顺其自然地前行，完成任务，享受你正在做的事情。

然后，事情发生了。

你走到了人生的一个自然阶段的终点，无论是学业阶段的结束，还是你可能为之工作的公司的终结，亦或是你人生某个时期的结束，你的配偶搬家了，总之发生了什么事，你的生活被打乱了。

而正是在这个时候，人们往往会陷入困境，他们没有足够的资源去仔细、系统、深入地思考，接下来到底应该做些什么，才能让自己的人生变得更加充实。

所以这就是我创建这门课程的原因。

我认为不同的人会在不同的时间获得不同的见解。

我要求我的学生每年写一篇期末论文，内容仅仅是他们对成功的个人看法以及他们打算如何实现这些目标的想法。

但我告诉他们，如果他们在10年后写出同样的论文，他们很可能会写出一篇不同的论文，可能性非常大。

他们会对自己在那个阶段是谁、下一步该做什么产生不同的想法，会有不同的经历可以借鉴，会与那些激励过他们、为他们提供了以前没有的榜样的人建立不同的关系。

所以，这门课程与其说是要给你答案，不如说是要给你一种思考问题的方式，让你能够找到自己的答案。

当然，这个问题本身就是一个大问题。

我所说的“成功”究竟是什么意思？

很好。

那么，我期待着我们稍后在我们开始下一节课时再次见到你。

英文原文

I teach this course because in my own life I found,especially in my education,that there wasn't really a single place I could go to learn about how to think about success.

Success is a huge,potent word in our culture.

Everybody wants more of it,but nobody's really quite sure what it means.

And most of the time,when everything's going great,you don't even think about it.

You're cruising along and getting things done and enjoying whatever you're doing.

And then something happens.

You come to the end of a natural course in your life,whether it's the end of a school section or the end of a company that you might be working for or the end of a period of your life,your spouse moves,something happens,and you're disrupted.

And very often that's when people sort of fall back and they don't have the resources to think carefully,systematically,thoughtfully about what they really ought to do next to bring their life to a more fulfilling place.

So that's why I created the course.

I think different insights come to different people at different times.

I ask my students to write a final paper every year that it's just their thoughts about what their personal views on success are and how they intend to achieve them.

But I tell them that the chances are pretty good that if they wrote the same paper 10 years later,they would probably write a different paper.

They would have different ideas about who they are at that stage and what they ought to do next,different experiences to build on,different relationships with people that have inspired them and given them role models that they didn't have before.

So this is not a course that's going to give you the answers as much as it's going to give you a way for thinking about the question so that you can find your answers.

And of course the question is the big one.

What do I mean by the word success?

Great.

So I'll look forward to seeing you again in a moment when we start our next session.

1-01-01.05_关于成功的三个真相

在这一节课中，我们将讨论关于成功的三个真相，我希望随着课程的进行，你能够逐渐理解并接受它们。

这是三个非常重要但人们常常感到困惑的事情。

那么，第一个实际上是三者中最重要的。

人们，因为他们读过关于成功的书籍或看过相关电影，会产生一种印象，认为成功存在某个单一的秘诀，认为只要他们能够发现这个秘诀，就能回答所有的问题，所有的问题都会迎刃而解，从此以后生活将是一帆风顺的美好体验。

而关于成功的真相则要复杂得多。

它不是一个秘诀。

它之所以复杂，是因为这些问题的答案存在于你的内心，而不是你身外的某个地方。

而且我认为，对于我们人类来说，如果只是把自己置于一个寻求的过程中，然后去寻找最高的山峰或最奇异的植物，然后我们就可以说，好吧，我们找到了，我们成功了，这样总是更简单。

不幸的是，成功是你随身携带的东西。

有一位名叫拉姆·达斯的作者写过一本很棒的书。

书名叫作《不论你去向何方，你就在那里》。

当谈到成功时，我认为这比说成功在某处更接近真相。

所以，没有秘诀。

这一切都将是你自己在内心发现的东西，我认为这会让你对自己正在努力追求的目标有更高的信心。

为了强调这一点，第二个真相是，与其说这是一场发现的探索，不如说这是一场认出的探索，去认出你内心已有的模式，去认出你正在努力实现的价值观。

这些价值观可能来自你的家庭，可能来自你的文化，可能来自某种宗教，而认出它们意味着理解并发现那些熟悉的、有价值的东西，比如说，对他人的同情心。

认出你曾被教导过这些，但在你努力爬上梯子顶端或治愈某种可怕疾病的过程中，你有点忘记了它。

现在你有了机会去思考并意识到，嗯，你知道吗？

我看到了我内心的那个价值观。

我现在可以用不同的方式来尊重它。

这并不意味着你必须停止寻找治愈疾病的方法。

这只是意味着你带着这个价值观，无论它可能是什么，同情心只是一个例子。

你随身携带着它。

这样做并不需要花费额外的时间。

当你这样做的时候，它只是给你的关系带来更深的理解。

所以，这关乎认出，而不是去寻找你从未想过的新事物。

然后，我希望随着课程的进行我们能揭示的第三个真相是，不存在任何一种每次都能奏效的、万无一失的技巧，可以用来实现你所决定拥抱的任何成功价值观。

在“如何成功”这个市场上，如果你走进任何一家书店，上网用谷歌搜索“成功”这个词，你会发现海量的关于如何成功的书籍，而且几乎所有这些书都会提供一个单一正确路径的模板。

这个单一正确路径可能是设定目标。

这个单一正确路径可能是社交技能。

这个单一正确路径可能是心智力量和可视化，以及运用你的想象力将事物变为现实的力量。

同样，所有这些事情可能都完全相关，它们可能对你非常有用，但你很可能会将它们与你独特的个人经历和能力结合起来，形成自己独特的组合，并以此为基础发展。

那个住在你隔壁、需要学习如何设定目标的人有效的方法，对你不一定有效，因为你已经每天设定了200个目标，而你正试图弄清楚如何放松下来，专注于三个目标。

所以，没有每次都奏效的万无一失的技巧，但有很多技巧。

你的目标是尝试为自己调整那些对你特别有效的工具，以实现你无论什么样的成功目标。

这些目标可能是内在的目标，可能是外在的目标，或者两者的结合。

我认为随着课程的进行，你会更深刻地理解这两者是如何相互作用的，以及它们是如何相互融合、相互整合的。

因此，我们将在下一节课中探讨其中的一些问题。

英文原文

In this session,we're going to talk about three truths about success that I hope you'll come to terms with as the course goes along.

These are three very important things that often people get confused about.

So,the first is really the most important of the three.

people,because they've read books or seen movies about success,have the impression that there is some single secret to success,that if they're only able to uncover it,that it'll answer all their questions,all the problems will be resolved,and that life will be a completely rosy experience from there on.

And the truth about success is much more complicated.

It's not a secret.

It's complicated because the answer to these questions lies within you,not outside you.

And I think it's always simpler for we humans if we can just put ourselves on a quest and then go look for the tallest mountain or the most exotic plant,and then we can say,well,we found it,we're successful.

Unfortunately,success is something that you carry with you.

There's a wonderful book by an author named Ram Das.

The title of the book is,No Matter Where You Go,There You Are.

And when it comes to success,I think that's more of the truth than that it's out there someplace.

So no secrets.

This is all going to be stuff that you find on your own in yourself that I think will give you a higher sense of confidence in what it is that you're striving toward.

Just to underline that,the second truth is that this is not a quest of discovery as much as it is a quest to recognize,to recognize the patterns that you already have within you,to recognize the values that you're striving to accomplish.

These values may come from your family,they may come from your culture,they may come from a religion,and recognizing them means understanding and finding the familiar,the value of,say,compassion for others.

Recognizing that you were taught that,but that you sort of forgot it in your quest to get to the top of the ladder or to cure some dread disease.

And you now get a chance to think and go,well,you know what?

I see that value inside me.

I now can honor it in a different way.

And it doesn't mean you have to stop looking for the cure for the disease.

It just means that you bring this value,whatever it might be,compassion's an example.

You bring it along with you.

Doesn't take any more time to do that.

It just brings a deeper understanding to your relationships when you do it.

So it's about recognition,not about finding new things you've never thought of.

And then the third truth that I hope we'll uncover as the course goes along is that there are no single foolproof techniques that work every time to achieve whatever the success value is that you've decided to embrace.

In the how to succeed market,if you go into any bookstore,go online and look at Google the word success,you're going to find just boatloads of books on how to succeed,and almost all of them are going to provide this template of one true path.

The one true path may be goal setting.

The one true path may be social skills.

The one true path may be mind power and visualization and the power of your imagination to bring things into reality.

Again,all these things may be perfectly relevant and they may be very useful to you,but the chances are pretty high that you're going to use your own unique combination of them with your own unique experiences and capabilities to build on them.

And what works for the person who lives next door to you,who needs to learn how to set goals,will not work for you because you already set 200 goals a day and you're going to be trying to figure out how to relax and focus on three goals.

So no foolproof techniques every time,but lots of techniques.

Your goal is to try to adapt for yourself the tools that will work uniquely well for you to achieve whatever your success goals are.

They may be internal goals,they may be external goals,or a combination of the two.

I think as the course goes on,you're going to get a richer sense of how those two play against each other and sort of fold in and integrate with each other.

So we'll be addressing some of these issues in our next session.

1-01-01.06_六种人生练习

在沃顿商学院教授成功学课程时，我们做的其中一件事是提供给学生一些练习、思维谜题、以及小的课后任务，让他们能够思考自己的成功价值观、自己的情感以及自己的能力。

然后当我们聚在一起时，我们会讨论人们得到的各种不同答案。

在这个在线课程环境中，我们要做的是为你提供相同的练习，并给你机会去完成它们。

然后我会回来，并能够与你分享我从这些练习中收到的一些典型回答，这些回答可能来自课堂，可能来自与高级管理人员一起的高管课程，也可能来自线上，那里有成千上万的人参与了其中一些评估。

通过这种方式，你将有机会将自己的答案作为参照，并根据这些其他回答来思考它们。

那么，让我们开始第一个练习吧。

这就是我们在沃顿成功学课程的第一节课上使用的练习。

我称它为“六种人生练习”。

它其实非常简单。

这里有六个简短的段落，每一段讲述了一个在不同职业环境中的个人的故事。

你需要阅读每一段文字。

大概就是，如果你把它打印出来，它会印在一张纸的正反两面。

然后思考这六个故事。

最后的部分将为我们提供一些可以讨论的内容。

我需要你按照你所认为的成功程度，将这些人生从第一名，即最成功的人生，排到第六名，即最不成功的人生。

我们尽量让每一种人生都有一个唯一的排名，所以不允许出现并列。

所以你会读到这六个简短的小故事。

你会思考它们，然后你对它们进行排名。

第一名是最成功的，依次往下到第六名，是最不成功的。

然后带着你的答案来到我们讨论其中一些背景情况的课程。

我想你会开始看到，当涉及到我们将要研究的这个神奇的词——“成功”时，这个练习是如何帮助你触及自己内心一些隐含的价值观的。

那么，花点时间，完成这个练习，我一会儿就回来讨论你的结果。

1-01-03.01_六种人生练习分析

在这一节中，我们将讨论你对“六种人生”练习的回答。

我曾在许多不同的场合，向成千上万的人讲授过这个练习，我有一些数据可以和你们分享，关于他们的结果，以及人们与我分享的一些观点，关于他们将某个人生排得很高或很低的原因。

如果你还没有机会做“六种人生”练习，没关系。

直接进入下一节，等你做完练习后再回来听这一节。

那么，这里介绍了六个不同的人，我将依次谈论每一个，并分享一些关于排高和排低的观点，即那些把这个人生活排在第一位的人，或者把它排在第六位的人。

如果你没有把它排在最高或最低，你可以问问自己，它是在你列表的顶部附近还是底部附近，你或许能从中获得一些insights。

那么，列表上的第一个人生是教师。

教师，如果你把教师选为你心目中的第一人生，我认为这通常表明你对于成为一名导师，在一个小环境中工作，真正去指导他人，激发他们的卓越潜能，抱有非常热情的看法。

你与人打交道，你在学校里工作，指导聪明的学生赢得科学奖项，这种前景对某些人来说感觉非常满足。

然而，有时人们会把这个人生活排在最后，因为，你记得故事里，作为教师的那个人有一个孩子，已经与家庭疏远了。

他们不再联系，孩子对他们伸出的援手没有回应，感觉在这个故事的家庭生活中出现了某种裂痕，人们非常不愿意认为这是一种成功的人生。

有时，指出这个因素的人觉得，教师的人生在某种意义上有点不完整，他们似乎能够全身心投入到帮助他人和工作中，但当涉及到自己的家庭生活和自己的孩子时，他们却没能把那种联结感带回家中。

而那些把这个人生活排高的人，则看着这个因素说，嗯，孩子变得疏远，其实并不是教师本人的选择，所以他们不会因此过多地苛责。

我认为，对于所有这些人生，你会发现，你自己的经历往往在很大程度上影响你把哪个排在更靠近顶部或更靠近底部。

比如，兄弟姐妹，或者一个不再与家庭来往的孩子，如果你在这方面的经历非常痛苦，那么你很可能就会把那个人生推到最底部。

另一方面，如果你认识的人，甚至你自己，曾经历过一段关系破裂但后来找到方法重归于好的时期，那么我认为你会更相信修复过程，那个人生中的那个部分，感觉像是可以解决的问题。

所以，至少，如果你把它排得很高，可以把它看作一个信号，表明你的动机是在较小的群体中工作，去影响他人的生活，去发掘他人的才能。

第二个人生，是银行家。

银行家是一位单身女性，带着一个患有严重残疾的孩子。

她的生活中没有伴侣，成年伴侣，她是一位专注、忠诚的专业人士，在财富管理领域拥有相当成功的职业生涯。

她把自己的家庭状况变成了一种财富，因为她成为了一名马拉松跑者。

她利用自己的跑步，为残疾儿童的事业贡献一份力量。

她用一种特殊改装的装置，推着她的孩子一起跑马拉松，并为这项事业获得公众关注。

所以，把这个人生活排在第一的人，常常赞赏这个人的自主性，她的选择。

她所有的朋友都说，她应该把孩子送到疗养院或福利机构，然后继续过自己的生活。

而她的反应是，不，不，这就是我的生活。

这为我提供了意义。

所以，你能感受到她所采取立场的勇气，以及她对这一立场的确定和自信。

把这个人生活排得很低的人，则把拥有一个严重残疾孩子的负担方面，视为这个人生活的一个决定性特征，感觉有点太局限了。

他们觉得这不是他们会选择的人生，因为看起来她似乎不想结婚。

她将自己的一生奉献给了这一个人，感觉她的生活因此受到了限制。

所以，同样地，如果你最高的价值观之一是忠诚、对家庭的奉献，那么这个人生活看起来就更有吸引力一些。

如果你更多考虑的是自主性、职业，或者拥有很多选择、能够广泛旅行等等的人生，那么这个人生活看起来就不那么好。

所以，你知道，它们没有正确或错误的答案。

它们只是人们在回答这些问题时，所引出的不同价值观而已。

那么，第三个人生是富有的投资人。

现在，在所有人生中，富有的投资人这个人是拥有，首先，最多的自主性。

这个人在职业生涯早期的一次投资中赚了一大笔钱。

然后，他们能够转而投资这些钱，为自己提供从事各种爱好和事业的手段。

他们喜欢悬挂式滑翔。

他们的生活中充满旅行，拥有很多自由。

他们甚至能参与政治事业。

所以，他们会把一部分钱捐给他们信仰的政治事业。

因此，他们在自己小小的亲密圈子之外，对周围的世界产生了很大的影响。

把这个人生活排得很低的人，没有关注那些自由和自主性，反而看着这个人生活说，这个人看起来很孤独。

他们结过婚。

但没成。

他们再也没有再婚。

他们没有孩子。

从故事中也看不出他们有家庭。

所以，对人们来说，这里缺失了一大块。

现在，再次地，我最近确实收到一位MBA学生的邮件，她选了这个人生活，并说这个人生活对她非常有吸引力，因为自由是她最珍视的价值观，高于其他一切。

你知道，她来到沃顿，实际上来自一个并不总能理所当然地拥有自由的国家。

所以当她来到这里时，这个人生活感觉非常有吸引力。

另一方面，其他人把这个人生活排在底部，是因为没有家庭，没有家庭，孤独，一种情感上的缺失。

好的，这是第三个人生。

继续，第四个人生，石匠。

从很多方面来看，石匠的人生与富有的投资人的人生是相反的。

这是一个有家庭的男人，与同一个伴侣结婚几十年，有孩子，其中一些孩子从事着与他完全不同的职业。

他用石头建造房屋。

他的孩子们则成了律师等等。

他用几乎是神秘的语言描述自己的生活。他认为自己的一天在很大程度上由自己掌控。

他有一种工匠般的能力，能够找到恰到好处的石头，并将其放在恰到好处的位置。

他为自己的孩子们建造了房屋，他可以开车穿过小镇，看到自己建造的房屋。

所以，这个人生活中充满了连贯性。

而把它排在靠近顶部的人，倾向于赞赏那种对家庭的拥抱，对技艺的拥抱，对掌控自己生活体验的拥抱。

它非常整合。

把它排在靠近底部的人，常常认为这个人生活规模很小。

这个人只能影响他的家庭。

他们只能通过他建造的房屋，影响社区里的少数人，而他们想要对世界产生更大的影响。

此外，这个人的技能似乎没有得到外界的认可。

甚至都没有像《石匠周刊》颁发的“本周石匠”这样的奖项。

他只是一个建造相当不错房屋的普通人。

所以，同样地，如果你的成功价值观更倾向于家庭、倾向于整合，那么这个人生活就会排得很高。

如果它们更倾向于对他人的影响、规模，以及某种自主性和选择，那么这个人生活看起来就不那么有吸引力了。

曾经有一位高管，就这个人生活向我发表过评论，因为在课堂上，我可能会选一个把它排在第一的人，描述他们为什么喜欢它，再选一个把它排在第六的人，描述他们为什么不喜欢。

那是在一个很大的群体里，房间里有一百个人，有个人刚刚用相当轻蔑的言辞描述了石匠，解释了为什么把他排在第六位。

这时，一个男人从房间后面站了起来，我想他有着非常深厚的精神背景，因为他站起来说，石匠对社会产生了巨大的影响。

石匠在建造房屋的同时，也在建造社会，他是他家庭的基石。

所以，这是对这个人生所蕴含的意义和象征意义的一种非常诗意的看法。

总之，这是一个在做练习时，会引发人们许多不同情绪的人生。

第五个人生是网球职业选手。

在所有不同的人生中，网球职业选手是唯一一个真正登上过杂志封面的人。

很明显，她在职业巡回赛中是一位非常有成就的选手，并且因为这个非常重要的成就而获得了认可和赞誉，因此，她拥有这种传统意义上的成功，被非常、非常清楚地描绘和定义。

她也有家庭，有伴侣。

他们无法拥有自己的孩子，所以她领养了孩子。

她还经营着一个小的网球训练营，给贫困儿童提供体验网球和学习相关技能的机会。

所以，喜欢这个人生活的人，把它排得更高，常常是关注所有这些属性，并对她为自己生活带来的事物组合抱有非常积极的感觉。

另一方面，把它排在靠近底部的人，则指向这个简短描述的其他方面，其中之一是她抱怨说，她因为职业太忙，没有时间像她希望的那样多陪伴孩子，因为她必须到处巡回比赛。

他们认为这可能是她在工作与生活平衡方面遇到的困难。

她没有选择正确的优先事项。

然后，你知道，有一种感觉，故事是这样写的，虽然没有明说，但这个人可能没有选择网球。

可能她只是虎妈或狼爸家庭的产物，他们在她小时候不断地训练她、训练她、训练她，她没有选择，只能这么做。

然后她刚好有这方面的天赋，变得非常擅长网球。

但这种她没有自己选择的感觉，对某些人来说没有吸引力。

他们觉得她更像一个受害者，也许，而不是一个成功者。

所以，取决于故事的哪一部分能引起你的共鸣，你可能会把它排得更高或更低。

六个人生中的最后一个是非营利组织高管。

非营利组织高管有其独特的特点。

首先，这个人在金融领域拥有成功的职业生涯，现在转向了非营利环境，为一个宗教团体工作，这个团体拥有他们非常坚定的信仰体系。

所以，他们正在将自己的专业技能重新用于一个更伟大的事业。

这对某些人有吸引力。

此外，他们现在正将注意力转向非洲一个非常重要的事业：非洲农村村庄的清洁水问题。

他们即将带着全家去那里，领导这项工作，处理这个项目，帮助他人。

这对那些想要在世界上产生影响、行善的人来说，感觉非常有吸引力。

把这个人生活排在底部的人，再次关注故事的不同部分。

他们看到了所有那些。

但是，这个人要带着孩子，其中一些还在上高中，离开他们的社交环境。

他们不想去。

而他无论如何都要带着配偶和他们一起去非洲。

他们认为，这就像一个即将在非洲农村爆炸的家庭定时炸弹，根本不是你会定义为成功的事情。

所以，同样地，取决于你的希望、恐惧和幻想，以及你的经历，你会关注这个人生的不同方面，要么喜欢它，要么不喜欢它。

我有一次非常有趣的经历。

我在波士顿和一个小组做这个练习，我们讨论完了所有的人生。

我请人们发言，问他们为什么选这个或那个。

前排一位年轻女士把非营利组织高管排在六个人生中的第六位。

我说，嗯，你觉得这个人生的有什么问题？

她说，非常激动地说。

嗯，我的父母都是福音派牧师。

他们去哪儿都拖着我们。

他们从来不在乎我们。

我绝不会为任何人选择这种人生。

你知道，大家都被她说话时的这种激动情绪所感染。

所以，这些人生活当然是无法评判的，因为它们描绘得非常简略。

因此，你实际上是在把你的人生故事读进每一个里面。

而取决于你人生故事中的哪些方面作为成功价值观产生共鸣，那些就是看起来有吸引力的人生。

那些是别人害怕、不会选择的人生。

那么，再补充一点视角，首先，你可能不会惊讶地知道，每次我给任何一组20人或更多的人做这个练习时，听众中总会有人把每个人生都选为第一，也总会有人把每个人生都选为第六。

这开始帮助你明白一点：成功并不是一个具有客观函数的东西。

这是你可以选择的东西，是你的看法、你的价值观、你的历史、你的经历、你的家庭，将成为你自己对成功人生构想的基石，因为它们都会被选中，而且人们对每个选择的感觉都同样强烈。

最后一点数据，仅供参考：我在网上做过这个练习，它可以在网上找到，成千上万的人做过。

基本上，有这么多人在线完成的结果，分成了三个层次，三组。

人们最常选的前两个人生是教师和石匠，并且它们并列。

不是一个高于另一个。

所以，人们似乎以某种方式珍视家庭部分、使命部分、自主部分，而这两个人生恰好体现了这些。

人们选择的最后两个人生，而且顶部和底部之间存在很大差距的，是富有的投资人和银行家。

我认为有趣的是，这两个人生都是家庭观念最淡薄的。

银行家没有家庭，我的意思是，不是没有，银行家家庭里只有一个人，但没有配偶，也没有结婚的意愿。

而富有的投资人没有孩子，没有配偶，也没有结婚的意愿。

所以，这是人们做出选择的一个决定性特征，而家庭似乎是人们深入思考成功时，实际权衡的最大因素之一。

然后，当然，非营利组织高管和网球运动员都处于中间区域。

但让我着迷的是它们是并列的。

基本上是顶部两个，中间两个，底部两个。

所以，你的答案是属于你的。

它们是有效的，最重要的是，试着从你选了哪些人生中，获得一些关于你自己的insights。

我想给你们最后一个我在这个练习结束时给学生的挑战，这可能会让你以不同的方式思考它，也可能不会。

这取决于你。

但让我问你们最后一个问题。

假设你死了，去了天堂，或者任何你能想象到的来世，你去办理进入永生，那里的神明满怀慈悲地看着你说，嗯，你知道，欢迎你，但我还有最后一个任务要交给你，你完成之后才能办理进入手续。

那就是这个。

你需要从六个人生练习中挑选一个人生，然后把它给你唯一的孩子。

那么，你现在面临的问题是：你会把哪个人生赋予你唯一的孩子，那个你希望给予最好的一切的人，你最在乎的人？

当我向人们提出这个问题时，通常多达一半的人，有时略多一点，会改变他们最初对第一的选择。

选择石匠的人，会把他们的选择改为教师，或者富有的投资人，或者其他人。

选择富有的投资人的人，会把他们的选择改为非营利组织高管，或者其他人。

我认为人们改变的原因，不是所有人都改，有些人坚持他们最初的选择，但他们改变选择的原因，是因为当你被要求把其中一个人生给你所爱的人，一个未来还有无限可能的人时，这不再只是一个关于你的理想是什么，或者理论上的完美成功图景是什么的问题，而是变成了你希望那个人拥有选择，你希望他们有财务安全，

你希望他们……我认为这是一个不同的问题，而且我认为这是一个更重要的问题，因为在你们每个人的内心深处，都有一个人在试图保护你，确保你的人生顺利，确保你做出的选择能让你蓬勃发展。

你不会只是随随便便地去过某种你认为理想或具有某种理论特性的人生，你是在挑选，是在做选择。

来支撑你走到下一个选择点。

所以，我认为这值得思考，因为很可能你实际上的成功理论，与这第二个问题关系更大，因为这将更准确地描述你在生活中实际做出的选择，而不仅仅是一个理论观点。

所以，当你思考这个练习时，我们在课程期间会定期回顾它，你可能需要正视你的价值观到底是什么，你的选择到底是什么，不要迷失在对某个你永远无法真正在其中做出选择的完美世界的迷雾中，要做出真实生活中的选择。那么至此，我们的第一个练习就结束了，现在我们要在下一节课中再深入一点，看看当你拆解成功时，会发生什么。

英文原文

In this session,we're going to talk about your answers to the Six Lives exercise.

I've taught this in many different contexts to thousands of people,and I've got some data that I can share with you about their results,as well as some perspectives that people have shared with me about their reasons for ranking one life or another,either very high or very low.

If you haven't had a chance to do the Six Lives exercise yet,no worries.

Just go on to the next session,and you can come back to this one after you've had a chance to do it.

So,there are six different people profiled here,and I'm just going to talk about each one in turn and share some perspectives on the sort of high and the low,the people who rank this life number one or the people who rank it number six.

And if you didn't rank it either one,you just ask yourself whether it was near the top of your list or near the bottom,and there might be some insights that you can gain from this.

So,the first life on the list is the teacher.

The teacher,if you chose the teacher as your number one life,I think it often signals a very passionate perspective on being a mentor,being involved in a small setting where you really get to coach people,bring out their excellence.

You're involved with people,you're involved in a school where you're coaching bright students to win science prizes,and that sort of perspective feels very satisfying to some people.

Sometimes,though,people pick this life last because,as you'll remember,in the story,the person who's the teacher has one child who has become estranged from their family.

They no longer are in contact,the child doesn't respond to efforts to reach out to them,and it feels like there's kind of fracture in the home life of this story,and people are very reluctant to endorse that as a successful life.

Sometimes the people who point to that factor feel that the teacher is a little bit of incomplete in the sense that they seem to be able to throw themselves at helping others and their work,but then when it comes to their own home life and their own children,they haven't been able to bring that same sense of connection to their home

The people who,again,pick the life on the high side look at that factor and say,well,it wasn't really the teacher's choice that the child would become disaffiliated,and so they don't count that against them as much.

I think with all these lives,what you're going to find is that your own experience tends to color a good deal which one you pick as closer to the top or closer to the bottom.

And the idea of a sibling.

Or a child that's no longer involved with the family,if your experience with that is very painful,then the chances are that you'll kind of push that one to the bottom.

On the other hand,if you know people or even yourself have had a period of your life where you're not reconciled but then have found a way to get back together again,then I think you are more of a believer in the healing process,and that part of that life feels like it's something that can be solved.

So,at the very least,if you ranked it high,consider this a sort of signal about your motivations for working in smaller groups to affect the lives of others and to bring out other people's talents.

Number two,life is the banker.

The banker is a single woman with a child who has a severe disability.

She has no partner in her life,adult partner,and is a dedicated,loyal professional with a rather successful career in wealth management.

She has turned her family situation into an asset as she has become a marathon runner.

She's used her running to facilitate sort of a cause for children with disabilities.

She wheels her kid with her on her marathon runs in a device that she's gotten specially rigged up and gets publicity for the cause.

So,people who pick this life number one often salute this person's autonomy,her choices.

All her friends are saying that she should put her child in a home or in a facility and get on with her life.

And her reaction is,No,no,this is my life.

This provides meaning for me.

And so,you feel the courage of the position that she's taken and her certainty and confidence in it.

People who pick this life down near the bottom see this sort of the burden aspect of having a child with a severe disability as a defining characteristic of this person's life as a little too narrow.

And they feel like this would not be a life they would choose because it seems she doesn't want to be married.

She devoted herself to this one person in her life,and it seems kind of restricted to them.

So,again,if one of your highest values is loyalty,devotion to family,then this life looks a little more appealing.

If you're thinking more about autonomy and a career or a life with lots of options and the ability to travel extensively and so on,this one doesn't look so good.

So,you know,none of them are the right or the wrong answer.

They're just different values that people elicit when they have to answer these questions.

So,life number three is the wealthy investor.

Now,I'm Among all the lives,the wealthy investor is the one who has,first of all,the most autonomy.

The person made a great deal of money on an early investment in their career.

They have then been able to turn to investing that money and to providing themselves with the means of carrying out all kinds of hobbies and causes.

They love hang gliding.

They have lots of travel in their lives,lots of freedom.

And then they can even get involved in political causes.

So they give some of their money to political causes that they believe in.

So they're having a lot of impact on the world around them outside of their little intimate sphere.

People who pick this life way down at the bottom,instead of focusing all the freedom and autonomy,look at this life and say,this person looks lonely.

They've been married.

It didn't work out.

They've never remarried.

They have no children.

They have no family that's discernible from the story.

And so there's this big missing piece for people.

Now,again,I actually got an email from an MBA student recently who picked this life and said that this life was very appealing to her because freedom is a value that she esteems above all others.

You know,she was from actually coming to Wharton from a country where freedom was not always an assumption that she could count on.

So when she got here,this life felt very appealing.

Other people,on the other hand,choose this life at the bottom because no family,no family,lonely,kind of an emotional deficit.

Okay,so that's number three.

Moving on to number four,the stonemason.

So in many ways,the stonemason's life is the opposite of the wealthy investor's life.

This is a man who has a family,has been married for decades to the same partner,has children,some of whom have gone on to do completely different careers than he has.

He builds homes with stone.

They've gone on to be lawyers and so on.

He describes his life in very almost mystical terms.He sees his day as very much under his control.

He has a kind of craftsman's-like ability to just find just the right stone and put it in just the right place.

He's built homes for his children and he can drive through his town and see the homes he's built.

And so there's a lot of coherence in this life.

And people who pick it near the top are inclined to salute that sort of embrace of family,embrace of craft,embrace of controlling the experience they're having in their life.

It's very integrated.

People who pick it down near the bottom often see this as a life with very Little scale.

This person is only affecting their family.

They're only affecting a few people in their community with the homes they build,he builds,and they want to have a bigger impact on the world.

Plus,there seems to be no recognition outside of this person to his skill.

So there's not even like an award from Stonemason Weekly that he was Stonemason of the Week.

He's just an average guy who builds pretty good homes.

So again,if your success values are more oriented toward the family,toward integration,then this one's going to rank very high.

If they're oriented more toward impact on others and scale,as well as a sort of autonomy and options,then this one doesn't seem quite as appealing.

I did have one executive once comment to me about this life because in a class I might pick one person who picked it number one and they described why they liked it and then one person who picked it number six and they described why they didn't.

And it was in a big group,100 people in the room,and someone had just described the Stonemason in rather disparaging terms and why they picked it number six.

And this man stood up in the back of the room and I think he was from a very strong spiritual background because he stood and said,the Stonemason is having a tremendous effect on society.

The Stonemason is building society as he builds his homes and that he is the foundation for his family.

So this very poetic view of the implications and the symbolism for this life.

Anyway,this is one that elicits a lot of different emotions from people when they take it.

Life number five is the tennis pro.

Now,the tennis pro of all of the different lives is the one person that is actually appeared on the cover of a magazine.

clear that she is a very accomplished professional on the circuit and has been acknowledged and recognized for this very important accomplishment and is so therefore has this sort of success in the traditional sense,very,very well outlined and defined.

She also has a family,partner.

They couldn't have children of their own,so she adopted children.

She has a little tennis camp that she's running that gives underprivileged kids a chance to experience tennis and learn the skills that come with that.

So people who like this life put it higher often focus on all those attributes and have a very positive feeling for the combination of things that she's bringing to her life.

On the other hand,people who rank it down near the bottom point to other aspects of this vignette,one of which is she complains.

That she's so busy with her profession that she doesn't have time to be with her kids as much as she would like because she has to be on the road.

They see this as maybe a difficulty in her work-life balance.

She's not choosing the right priorities.

And then,you know,there's a sense,the way the story is written,although it's not explicit,that maybe this person didn't choose tennis.

And it could just be that she was the product of a tiger mother or guerrilla father household,and they drilled her and drilled her and drilled her when she was a kid,didn't have a choice,she just had to do it.

And then she just had an aptitude for it and she got to be really good at tennis.

But the sense that she didn't choose it herself does not appeal to some people.

They feel like she's more of a victim,maybe,than a success.

So,depending on which part of that story resonates with you,you might have picked it higher or lower.

The final life of the six is the nonprofit executive.

The nonprofit executive has got its own unique features.

The first is that this person has had a successful career in finance and now has turned it and has gone into a nonprofit environment where they're working for a religious group,a very strong belief system that they have.

So they're repurposing their professional skills toward a greater cause.

That appeals to some people.

In addition,they are now turning their attention to a very important cause in Africa:clean water in villages in rural Africa.

And they're about to take their whole family over there and lead the effort to handle this initiative and help others.

That feels very appealing to some people who want to have an impact and do good in the world.

People who choose this life at the bottom,again,focus on a different part of the story.

They see all that.

But this person is taking children who,some of whom are in high school,away from their social environments.

They don't want to go.

He's taking them to Africa anyway with his spouse.

And they feel this is just a time bomb of a family about ready to explode in rural Africa and not at all something that you would define as successful.

So again,depending on your hopes,fears,and fantasies,as well as your experience,you focus on different aspects of this life and either favor it or disfavor it.

I had a very interesting experience.

I did this exercise with a group up in Boston,and we got through all the lives.

I was calling on people and asking them why they chose one or the other.

And a young lady who was in the front row had picked a nonprofit executive as the sixth out of six lives.

And I said,well,what was the problem for you with this life?

And she said,Very passionately.

Well,my mother and father were both evangelical ministers.

They dragged us everywhere they went.

They never cared about us.

I would never choose this life for anybody.

And,you know,everybody was sort of taken with this passion that she spoke with.

So these lives are impossible to judge,of course,because they're very sketchily drawn.

And so what you're really doing is reading your life story into each of them.

And depending on what aspects of your life story resonate as success values,those are the lives that seem to be the ones that are appealing.

Those are the ones for others who fear them and don't choose them.

So just for some additional perspective,first,you may not be surprised to know that every single time I give this exercise to any group of people of 20 or more,there is someone in the audience who chooses each of the lives as number one,and there is someone in that audience who chooses each of those lives as number six.

So this begins to help you see the point that success is not something that has an objective function.

This is something you get to choose,and it's your perceptions,your values,your history,your experience,your family that is going to be the foundation for your own vision of what a successful life is,because they all get picked and people feel equally strongly about each of them.

Just one last bit of data for what it's worth is:I've given this online to,it's available online and thousands of people have taken it.

And it basically,the results online with that many people taking it have fallen into three tranches,three sets.

The top two lives that people pick most often are the teacher and the stonemason,and they're tied.

It's not one over the other.

So people seem to value the family part,the mission part,the autonomy part in some way that those two lives embody.

The bottom two lives that people pick,and this is a big gap between the top and the bottom,are the wealthy investor and the banker.

And I think it's interesting that both of those lives are the ones with the most pared-down vision of family.

The banker has no family,I mean,not the banker has one person in their family,but no spouse and no interest in marrying.

And the wealthy investor has no children and no spouse and no interest in marrying.

So there is a defining feature of the choices people are making,and family seems to be one of the biggest Factors that people weigh when they actually give success some deeper thought.

And then,of course,the nonprofit executive and the tennis player both occupy the middle zone.

But it fascinates me that they're tied.

They're basically two at the top,two in the middle,two at the bottom.

So,your answers are yours.

They are valid,and the most important thing is to try to gain some insight about yourself from which ones you picked.

I just want to give you one last challenge that I give to my students at the end of this exercise,and it may cause you to think about it differently or not.

It depends.

But let me give you one last question.

Suppose that you died and went to heaven,or whatever afterlife you can imagine,and you went to check in to the everlasting life,and the deity there looked on you with compassion and said,Well,you know,welcome,but I have one final task for you that you have to do before you're allowed to check in,

And that is this.

You need to take one of the six lives in the six lives exercise,and you need to give it to your only child.

So,the problem you now face is:which of these six lives would you endow to your only child,the person you would want the best for,the person that you care the most about?

And when I put that question to people,very often as many as half of them,sometimes a little more,change their vote for number one.

People who voted for the stonemason change their vote to the teacher or to the wealthy investor or someone else.

People who voted for the wealthy investor change their vote to the nonprofit executive or someone else.

And I think the reason that people change,not all do,some people stick with the same vote they had at the beginning,but the reason they change their vote is because when you're asked to give one of these lives to someone you love who has a life in front of them,

it stops being a question of just what's your ideal or what's sort of the perfect picture of success in a theoretical way and becomes something where you want the person to have options,you want them to have financial security,you want them to beAnd I think that's a different question,and I think it's a more important one because inside each of you,there is someone who is trying to protect you and make sure that your life works and make sure that you make choices that will allow you to prosper.

And you're not just going off and living some life that you think is ideal or has some theoretical properties,you're picking and making choices.

to sustain you to the next choice point.

And so I think it's worth thinking about because the chances are that your actual theory of success has more to do with this second question because that will describe more accurately the actual choices that you're making in your life and not just a theoretical point.

So as you contemplate this exercise,and we'll come back to it periodically during the course,you might just come to terms with what your values actually are,what your choices actually are,and don't get lost in the fog of thinking about some perfect world that you could never actually make choices in,

make real life choices So with that,we've come to the end of our first exercise,and now we're going to dig deeper a little bit into the next session and see what happens to success when you unpack it.

1-01-03.02_成功的两个方面

当你第一次拆解“成功”这个词时，它就像一个盒子，你打开盒子往里面看，首先注意到的是，你可能在“六种人生”练习中也注意到了这一点，因为无论你读的是哪种人生，它们都包含了这两个维度。

所以，当你打开盒子往里看时，你会发现盒子里还有两个盒子。

我把其中一个盒子称为“外在生活”，另一个盒子称为“内在生活”。

外在生活与成就、职业、认可、名声、他人的尊重、你所扮演的角色以及你找到的社会职业有关。

而外在生活，是大多数人仅仅听到“成功”这个词时就会想到的东西。

他们会想，哦，某人成功了。

这意味着，他们是，你知道的，他们银行的行长，或者他们大学毕业了，或者他们有什么发明创造之类的。

所以，外在生活是媒体报道的对象。

外在生活是杂志颂扬的对象。

外在生活是人们获得奖项的原因。

正因如此，每个人通常，不是每个人，但人们通常认为成功就只有这些。

然而，这里有一个难题，因为如果你在街上随便找个人，随便问他们，我有时会这么做，因为这是我的专业领域，而且在杂货店排队，前面的人正数着零钱买水果沙拉时，我想打发时间，我就会问某人，你知道，我在做一个小调查。

你认为成功意味着什么？

如果他们愿意回答问题，并且不觉得我太古怪，那么他们几乎总是倾向于说，嗯，我不知道。

在我看来，成功就是快乐。

如果你快乐，你就成功了。

如果你问某人，你对自己孩子的目标是什么？

几乎所有人都会说，嗯，我们只希望他们快乐。

所以一方面，从社会的角度来看，外在生活这个盒子里，我们所颂扬的都是成就、职业、职位和地位。

而另一方面，你还有内在生活，这另一部分，是大多数人在思考他们真正在乎什么时，最终会归结到的东西。

因此，成功的这两方面之间存在着矛盾。

而我们在这门课程中将要一起做的很多事情，以及你在未来的人生旅程中将要尝试在自己的生活中解决的很多事情，就是协调、整合和平衡外在生活与内在生活。

以及你如何评价自己拥有一个内在丰富或在外部获得高度认可的人生，以及这两者之间会发生什么。

我认为，很多时候我们在生活中做出的选择都偏向于外在生活，然后我们会感到后悔和疑虑，因为我们在内在生活上有所欠缺。

我认为有时候选择内在生活而非外在生活是困难的，因为它看起来如此不重要。

但当然，你知道，在你生命的尽头，我想大多数人都会相当倾向于认为，他们不会说，哎呀，我真希望能再活一天，这样我就能多工作一会儿。

我想他们很可能会希望再活一天，这样他们就能和他们所爱的人多待一天。

所以，成功的这两个方面将贯穿我们整个课程，而你如何看待它们，将是我们分析、拆解和思考我们所讨论的所有不同主题时的一个重要主题。

那么，在下一节课中，我们将探讨一些与我们目前所讨论内容相关的主题。

英文原文

When you unpack the word success for the first time,it's like a box,and you open the box and you look inside,the first thing you notice,and you probably noticed this in the Six Lives exercise,because no matter which life you were reading,each of them had these two dimensions.

So when you open the box and look inside,what you find is two boxes inside the box.

I call one box the outer life and the other box the inner life.

The outer life has to do with achievements,career,recognition,celebrity,respect from others,the roles you play and the social occupations that you found your way to.

And the outer life is what most people think of when they just hear the word success.

They think,oh,someone's successful.

It means that they are,you know,the president of their bank,or they graduated from college,or they have some sort of invention that they made or something.

So the outer life is what the media covers.

The outer life is what magazines celebrate.

The outer life is what people get awards for.

And for that reason,everybody often,not everybody,but people often think that that's all it is.

then there's this conundrum because if you take an average person on the street and you just ask them randomly,which I sometimes do just because it's my field and I'm trying to kill time in a grocery store line while someone's counting pennies at the very beginning of the line to pay for their fruit salad,

I ask somebody,you know,I'm doing a little survey.

What do you think success means?

And if they're willing to answer the question and they don't think I'm too weird,then they will be almost always inclined to say,well,I don't know.

It seems to me like success is happiness.

If you're happy,you're successful.

And if you ask somebody,what's your goal for your children?

Almost all of them would say,well,we just want them to be happy.

So on the one hand,you've got this societal point of view of the box of the outer life where all that we celebrate is achievements and career and position and status.

And on the other hand,you have this inner life,the other part,which is what most people resort to when they kind of think about what they really care about.

And so there's this contradiction between these two sides of success.

And a lot of what we're going to do together in this course and that you will be trying to resolve in your own life as you go through your life is reconciling and integrating and balancing the outer life and the inner life.

and the credit you give yourself for having a life that is rich in its inner dimensions or highly recognized in its outer dimensions and what happens between those two.

I think it's often the case that we make choices in our lives that favor the outer life and then we have regrets and second guessing because we've come up short on the inner life.

I think it's hard to choose the inner life over the outer life sometimes because it looks so unimportant.

But of course,you know,at the end of your life,I think most people are pretty inclined to think that they would not say,gee,I wish I could have another day to be alive so I could work some more.

I think they're probably going to be asking themselves for another day so they could be with the people they love for another day.

So these two sides of success are going to be with us throughout the course and how you consider them a big theme in how we're going to analyze,break down,and think about all the different topics that we talk about.

So in our next session,we'll be picking up some themes related to everything we've talked about so far.

1-01-03.03_文化与家庭在设定成功价值观中的作用

我们已经讨论过成功这个盒子，以及在这个盒子里，你会发现另外两个盒子：内在生活的快乐与满足，以及外在生活的职业、地位和成就。

但你可能会问自己，这个盒子是怎么被填满的？

是谁把这一切放进去的？

当你开始思考成功对你究竟意味着什么时，你必须深入探究的下一个、也是最重要的层面，就是这些价值观的来源。

你会立刻面对一个非常、非常重要的价值观的文化来源。

在任何一个特定的文化中，你的家庭就像一面棱镜，会将弥漫于文化中的某些价值观聚焦，投射到你的家庭里，最终形成你的一套固有观念：关于你应该做什么，什么重要、什么不重要，什么会为你赢得赞扬，什么会招致失望。

所以，文化和家庭，是两个非常重要的因素，而且非常难以处理。

有一位小说家，大卫·福斯特·华莱士，一位现代小说家，在2005年肯扬学院的毕业典礼上发表过演讲。

他讲了一个故事，我认为这个故事说明了为什么这是一个如此难以把握的主题。

故事里说，有一条老鱼在水里游着。

有两条年轻的鱼游过来，从他身边经过，往另一个方向去了。

当这两条年轻的鱼经过他身边时，老鱼对它们说，水怎么样啊？

这两条年轻的鱼因为被陌生人搭话而有点不高兴，也不知道该说什么，所以就继续往前游。

但大约游了十码远，其中一条年轻的鱼转向另一条年轻的鱼说，呃，水是什么？

这个问题，当然，正是那种年轻的鱼更难回答的问题，因为随着你年龄增长，经验越来越丰富，经历的生活事件越来越多，你就越会意识到，你正游弋在自己的文化之中，带着自己的文化预设，并且你被一生所沉浸的文化和家庭价值观所驱动着、所推动着，几乎是痴迷地寻求着它们的认可。

它们是你的一部分，就像你的心脏是你身体的一部分一样。

所以，将自己与那一切分离开来，获得一个观察它的视角，以便你能够接纳、调整或摒弃那些曾为你定义成功的文化和家庭价值观——这是学习这门课程、思考成功这个主题的旅程中一个非常重要的部分。

我为你准备的正是这个。

英文原文

So we've talked about the box that success is and that inside the box you find two other boxes,the inner life of happiness and fulfillment and the outer life of career,status,and achievement.

But you might ask yourself,how did this box get filled up?

Who put it all there?

And the most important next layer you have to penetrate as you begin thinking about what success really means to you is the sources of these values.

And you immediately confront a very,very important cultural source for the values.

And within any given culture,your family will be like a prism that will focus certain aspects of the cultural values that are sailing it to your families into your sets of assumptions about what you ought to be doing and what counts and what doesn't count and what will earn you praise or what will earn you disappointment.

So,culture and family,two really important things,and very difficult.

There was a novelist,David Foster Wallace,a modern novelist,who gave a commencement address at Kenyon College in 2005.

And he told a story that I think illustrates why this is such a difficult subject to get a grip on.

And in the story,he said that there was an old fish that was swimming along in the water.

And two teenage fish came swimming around and passed him going the other way.

And as the two teenage fish went by him,the old fish said to them,how's the water?

And the two teenage fish were a little upset with being spoken to by a stranger and they didn't really know what to do,so they just kept swimming.

But about 10 yards away,the one teenage fish turned to the other teenage fish and said to,well,what's water?

Now,that question,of course,is the kind of question that teenage fish would have more trouble answering because the older you get,the more experience you have,the more different life events have happened to you,the more you become aware that you're swimming in your own culture with your own cultural assumptions and that you are motivated by,impelled by,kind of almost obsessively seeking validation within the cultural and family values that you've been surrounded by your whole life.

They are part of you just the way that your heart is part of your body.

So separating yourself from that,getting perspective on that so that you can embrace,modify,reject the cultural and family values that have defined success for you,a very important part of the journey that studying this subject and thinking about success.

I have in store.

1-01-03.04_我的故事

我很小的时候就非常、非常深刻地意识到了这一点，但几乎是不由自主地。

但这也是为什么这个主题对我很重要，以及为什么我会教授它的一个重要原因。

我在军营里长大。

我的父亲是海军陆战队的一名将军。

我小时候，他每年都会调动到不同的地方，法国、夏威夷、南卡罗来纳州、罗德岛州的纽波特。

而我作为家庭的一份子，也跟着一起搬家。

我有两个姐姐和我。

那就是我生活的世界。

我们搬到的每个地方都有一个带警卫的基地。

而且据我所知，每个人都那样生活。

所以，随着我长大，问题不是我是否会从军作为我的职业，而只是我要上哪所军事院校，以及选择哪个军种的问题。

所以，当我进入高中，开始考虑大学时，我有点意识到自己真的既不想去西点军校，也不想去安纳波利斯海军学院，但我仍然完全致力于以军人为职业。

于是我最终和家人达成了一个妥协，我获得了另一所大学的全额军事奖学金，而不是去西点或安纳波利斯。

所以我就报名了。

我参加了海军后备军官训练团，并将在毕业后至少服役六年，成为一名海军军官。

一切都很正常。

我就像在自己的水域里顺畅地游着。

然后，在我上大学期间，正值越南战争时期。

而到了大学三年级，我周围的一切几乎都爆炸了。

美国入侵了柬埔寨。

全国的大学校园都燃起了抗议的怒火。

我自己的校园也停掉了所有的课程。

那是我生命中第一次，真的被召唤去对我报名要做的事情表明立场——而那一刻我意识到，那件事就是去杀害与我无冤无仇的越南人民。

我突然意识到，那是我绝对做不到的事情。

于是我面临着一个重大的选择。

我意识到，在这个时代、这个背景下，我无法认同我的家庭价值观，但我又爱我的家人。

所以我陷入了危机。

最终，我决定成为一名反战者。

我放弃了奖学金，但我不得不就我的选择与父亲进行一次非常艰难的谈话。

我进行了那次谈话。

他当时，并没有生我的气。

事实上，最让我难受的是，在我与他的谈话中，他只问了一个简单的问题。

他说，理查德，你确定吗？

而当时年仅21岁，背离了我家族所代表的一切的我，绝对无法确定。

那不仅仅是我父亲的问题。

我的祖父曾在军中服役。

我的外祖父也曾在军中服役。

我的姐姐嫁给了一位职业军官。

所以我完全被这些价值观包围着。

但在那一刻，面对他，我必须确定。

于是我说，是的，我确定。

而我当时不知道，并且花了我十多年才理清的是，当你以这种方式与家庭决裂，背离了你从小被灌输的、他们一直坚守的一切时，你会发现自己陷入了一种茫然若失的境地。

你基本上切断了自己人生故事的叙事纽带，你不再是曾经的你了。

你不再认得自己的童年。

我可以根据亲身经历告诉你，如果你没有过去，就不可能认识和想象未来。

于是我完成了大学学业。

我成为了一名依良心拒服兵役者，一名和平主义者，在华盛顿特区的贫民窟做社工，对于自己是谁、立场何在，非常非常不确定，除了仍然确信自己做出了正确的选择。

但我和自己的文化及家庭价值观之间的那种疏离感，最终导致我干脆离开了那个国家。

我花了将近两年时间，背着背包旅行，生活非常接地气，在我能免费工作或免费食宿的不同地方打工，只是想试着理清这一切。

在那两年里，我最后在斯里兰卡和韩国的寺院里生活过。

我有一些很棒的老师，他们引导我亲身体验了做自己，以及更深入地拥抱我逐渐认同的那些价值观。

终于，在快30岁的时候，我回家了。

我的家人欢迎我回来。

我住在他们家的地下室里，在弗吉尼亚州西南部挨家挨户推销保温材料，同时试图弄清楚下一步该做什么。

我认为，那段经历在很大程度上解释了为什么这门课程的材料对我来说如此重要，因为我认识到，直到我认清那些造就了我的文化力量，并掌控了自己的生活和价值观，为之挺身而出，拥抱它们，并将它们呈现给我的家人，我的家人爱我，无论我们有何分歧。

我很幸运能够陪伴我的父母，走过他们的一生，在他们临终时都陪在他们身边，并感受到了当你用心经营你的关系和家庭时，所产生的那种深沉的爱。

所以我觉得，人们迟早会以某种方式，去面对家庭赋予他们的价值观，面对文化赋予他们的价值观，并在通往理解成功含义的旅程中，把这些作为一个非常重要的中转站来接受和处理。

我之所以有这种感觉，是因为这就是我的经历。

我直到37岁才开始在沃顿工作。

那时我刚成为这里的一名助理教授。

所以，任何正在观看这个视频、觉得自己是大器晚成的人，请放心，很可能仍有足够的时间来理清这一切。

我真诚地相信，正确认识这一点，接受真实的自己，比总是过着别人的人生，却意识不到真正驱动你的是何种潜在动机，要重要得多。

所以分享这个故事。

我想，让你了解一些关于我是谁、我从何而来的信息很重要。

但这门课不是关于我的。

这门课是关于你的。

所以请理解，课程的结构旨在帮助你获得自己的领悟，接纳你自己的价值观，这样你就能在坚实的根基上，为你未来几年做出的决策奠定基础。

英文原文

I was someone who was very,very deeply aware of this at an early age,but almost involuntarily.

But it is a big reason why this subject is important to me and why I teach it.

I was raised in the military.

My father was a general in the Marines.

He was moved every year when I was a kid to a different place,France,Hawaii,South Carolina,Newport,Rhode Island.

And I was taken as part of our family.

I had two older sisters and me.

And that was just the world I was in.

Every place we moved had a base with a guard.

And as far as I knew,everybody lived like that.

And so as I grew up,it wasn't a question of whether I was going to go in the military as my career.

It was just a question of which military academy I would attend and which service I would pick.

So as I got into high school and began thinking about college,I kind of realized I really didn't want to go to either West Point or Annapolis,but I was totally committed to the military as a career.

So I ended up making a compromise with my family and I ended up getting a full military scholarship to another college,not to West Point or Annapolis.

So I was signed up.

I was in Navy ROTC and I was on my way to being an officer in the Navy for at least six years after I graduated.

Everything's normal.

I'm in my water swimming along.

And then I was in the Vietnam War era in my college years.

And in the junior year of college,everything around me virtually exploded.

The United States invaded Cambodia.

Campuses all over the country lit up with protests.

My own campus had shut down all of its classes.

And for the first time in my life,I was actually called to try to take a stand on what I had signed up to do,which at that moment I realized was to go kill Vietnamese people that I had no quarrel with.

And I suddenly realized that that was just something I couldn't do.

And so I faced a big choice.

I was realized that my family values were not things that I could endorse in this era,in this context,but I love my family.

So I was in a crisis.

In the end,I finally decided to become a war resistor.

I resigned my scholarship,but I had to have a very difficult conversation with my father about my choices.

And I had that conversation.

He was.Not angry with me.

In fact,the most upsetting thing about it for me was the fact that he only asked a simple question in my conversation with him.

He said,Richard,are you sure?

And I absolutely could not be sure at the age of 21 and walking away from everything my family had stood for.

It wasn't just my dad.

My dad's dad had been in the military.

My mother's father had been in the military.

My older sister had married a career military officer.

So I was surrounded by these values.

But with him at that moment,I had to be sure.

And so I said,Yes,I'm sure.

And what I didn't know at the time,and what took me over a decade to sort out,was that when you break with your family in this way and walk away from everything that you've been raised with,that they've stood for,you find yourself in a kind of limbo.

You essentially cut the narrative cord of your life story,and you're no longer the person that you were.

You don't recognize the childhood you had.

And I can tell you from first-hand experience that if you don't have a past,it's impossible to recognize and imagine the future.

So I finished college.

I became a conscientious objector,a pacifist,worked in the ghettos of Washington,D.C.as a social worker,very,very uncertain about who I was or where I stood,other than that I was still sure I'd made the right choice.

But the kind of alienation between me and my own cultural and family values was such that in the end I just left the country.

I spent almost two years traveling with a backpack,living very close to the ground,working in different places where I could work for free just to try to,or live for free,try to sort it out.

And over those two years,I ended up living in monasteries in Sri Lanka and in South Korea.

I had some wonderful teachers who introduced me to the actual experience of being myself and the values that I had come to embrace in a much more deep way.

And finally,at the age of almost 30,I returned home.

My family welcomed me back.

I lived in their basement and sold insulation door-to-door in southwestern Virginia while I tried to figure out what the next thing to do was.

And that experience,I think,is a lot of why this course material is so important to me because I recognized that until I had identified those cultural forces.

that I was living as a result of and taken control of my own life and my own values and stood up for them,embraced them,presented them to my family.

My family loved me irrespective of our differences.

I was actually privileged to be with them,my parents,all the way through their lives,was with them each when they died,and felt the deep love that comes when you work on your relationships and your family in important ways.

So I feel like sooner or later,one way or the other,people come to confront the values that their families have endowed them with,the values that their culture has endowed them with,and come to terms with those as a very important way station on the journey to what success means.

And I feel that way because it's the way it worked for me.

I didn't start working at Wharton until I was 37.

I was a brand new assistant professor here at that age.

So anybody who's watching this who thinks that they're kind of a late bloomer,rest assured that there's still probably plenty of time to sort this out.

I genuinely believe it's more important to get this right and to come to terms with who you really are than it is to always be living someone else's life and not be aware of the underlying motivations that are actually powering who you are.

So share that story.

I think it's important for you to know something about who I am and where I'm coming from.

But the course isn't about me.

The course is about you.

So just understand that the structure of this is designed to help you come to your own realizations and come to terms with your own values so that you can feel on a firm foundation for the decisions you make in the years ahead.

1-01-03.05_我们所处的位置与前进的方向

现在，我们花点时间总结一下目前的内容，并看看接下来要学习什么。

你已经开始了对自己成功价值观的探索。

你审视了那六种人生，并试图判断哪些你认为最成功，哪些最不成功。

你开始看到，在每一种人生中，外在生活——即地位、成就和职业，与内在生活——即快乐、满足感、爱、家庭之间，都存在一种平衡。

以及这两部分是在何处交汇融合，又或是彼此分离。

然后，我们探讨了其中一些价值观在你自身文化理解中的起源，你成长过程中被灌输的家庭价值观，也许还有你继承的精神或宗教价值观。

并且你开始认识到，存在一个时刻，你需要停下来审视这些价值观，决定你对待它们的态度。

你是全盘接受它们吗？

你需要调整它们吗？

你是否需要摒弃其中的某些部分，以便在自己的旅程中取得进展？

我们接下来要做的，是更详细地探讨，更详细地，有哪些独特的方法，能让你开始将自己视为一个能够取得成功的人，这些方法不是向外看，拿自己和别人比较，然后说，哦，和那个人相比，我是个失败者，或者我不如我这个榜样那么好。

而是要向内看，审视自己，好的，我今天处于什么位置？

我想在哪里投入精力，以便明天取得进步，并在你自身能力和兴趣的坚实基础上更上一层楼？

嗨，欢迎回到沃顿商学院的成功学课程。

我认为，每个人在开启理解成功意义的旅程时，迈出的第一步其实非常简单。

我对此有一个比喻。

就像醒来一样。

你知道，当你睡着的时候，你对周围发生的事情只有模糊的感知。

你会做梦，可能会不安，可能会辗转反侧，可能会意识到一些噪音，但就在某个时刻，你的意识突然开始扩展、扩展、再扩展，然后你睁开眼睛，砰的一声，你就进入了另一种意识状态。

你醒了。

我认为，当你在探寻自己成功价值观的旅程中，会发生这样的事：一些意外的信息输入，某人发表的评论，你听到的某次讲座，甚至是在这门课程里，你可能反思了某些说过的话并正在思考。

然后，就在顿悟的这一刻，你会恍然大悟，啊，原来这就是我一直困惑的地方。

而这一切可能发生在一瞬间。

我最近在教一个高管培训课程。

我们做了你们已经做过的“六个谎言”练习。

之后，一位女士眼含热泪走向我，因为她问我，那个最后的问题——你愿意把你唯一孩子的一生交付给哪一种——我是不是也问过她？

我说，是的，我对每个人都问了这个问题。

她说，嗯，在那之前，我选择了石匠的人生。

但当你问出那个问题时，我突然意识到，我真正想选的其实是教师的人生。

然后我才明白，石匠的人生一直是我父母希望我过的，而不是我自己想要的。

我可以看到她的眼中噙满了泪水，但随着她开始这个“唤醒”过程，去发现自己真正的价值观以及未来将何去何从时，她的整个思想都充满了能量。

所以说，文化、媒体和社会压力的催眠力量是无比巨大的。

而我始终完全尊重这种力量，因为人们要想逆流而上，顶住这些压力去发现并遵循自己所认同的价值观生活，是极其困难的。

在沃顿商学院，有很多很多学生来读我们的本科项目、MBA项目。

他们带着一整套价值观和抱负来到这里。

但在一个顶尖商学院的环境里，他们中的许多人常常能感受到一种社会共识，即某些职业，比如银行业或咨询业，被视为主要的、高地位的职业。

面对这种关于他人似乎都向往的目标的社会共识所带来的压力，人们很难保持自己的存在感、自己的方向，并坚持自己最初来这里的目标。

所以经常发生的情况是，他们会稍微绕个弯，毕业，做一些自己从未想过的事情，然后几年后，他们突然醒悟，回到自己以前拥有的价值观上，重新踏上自己的道路。

所以，你知道，这是一段充满曲折的旅程，但认识到、赞赏并尊重你所拥有的那些顿悟时刻，真的非常重要。

确保你有办法记住它们。

在课程后期，我们会讨论一些技巧，实际上是关于如何记住你的价值观，并让它们变得生动鲜明，这样你就能一遍又一遍地回归到这些价值观上来。

那么在下一节，我想给你讲个小故事，然后我们将一起探索，在你追求自身成功的过程中，你能带来哪些独特的东西。

Hi,welcome back to the Success Course here at Wharton.

I think the first step that everyone takes when they begin the journey of understanding the meaning of success is really simple.

And I kind of have a metaphor for it.

It's like waking up.

You know,when you're asleep,you're dimly aware of things that are going on.

You have dreams,you might be restless,you might toss and turn,you might be aware of noises,but then there's this moment when your consciousness just suddenly kind of expands,expands,expands,and then you open your eyes and boom,you're in a different form of consciousness.

You're awake.

And I think what happens when you are on a journey to discover what your success values are is some surprise input,some comment somebody makes,some lecture you hear,or even in this course you might reflect on something that has been said and that you're thinking about.

And there's this moment of insight and you go,ah,that's what I've been puzzled by.

And it can happen in a moment.

I was teaching an executive program recently.

We did the Six Lies exercise that you've already done.

And a woman afterwards came up to me and she had tears in her eyes because she was asking me had,I asked that last question,the question about which life would you give to your only child,had I asked that for her?

And I said,well,I ask it for everyone.

She said,well,up to that point,I'd chosen the Stonemason's life.

And then when you asked that question,I suddenly realized that I really would choose the teacher's life.

And I then realized that it was the Stonemason's life that my parents had always wanted for me and not the life that I wanted for myself.

And I could just see her eyes were filled with tears,but her mind was totally filled with energy as she began this wake-up process of discovering what her actual values are and where she'd take them from here.

So the hypnotic power of culture,media,social pressure is overwhelming.

And I always respect it completely because of the difficulty people have in swimming against those pressures to discover and then live by the values that they endorse.

Here at the Wharton School,many,many students come for our undergrad program,for our MBA program.

They come With a whole set of values and aspirations.

But within the context of a major business school,many of them often feel the social agreement about certain careers,whether it's in banking or consulting,as being the sort of primary high-status careers.

And against the social pressure of the social agreement of what everyone else seems to be aspiring to,it's very difficult for people to maintain their own presence,their own direction,and stay on course for what it is that they came here for.

So it often happens that they get a little detour,graduate,go do something they hadn't thought of,and then a couple of years later,they suddenly wake up and come back to those values that they'd had before and then set off on their path.

So it's,you know,it's a journey with many twists and turns,but it's really important to recognize,salute,and respect those moments of insight that you have.

Make sure that you have ways of remembering them.

Later in the course,we're going to talk a little about some techniques actually for remembering what your values are and making them vivid so that you kind of come back to them over and over again.

So in the next session,I want to tell you a little story,and then we'll be exploring some of the unique things that you bring to the table as you pursue your own success.

1-02-01.02_一则寓言

在成功学课程里，我们喜欢讲故事。

而我最喜欢的故事之一，其实就起源于我们所在的费城，宾夕法尼亚大学和沃顿商学院就坐落于此。

有一位名叫康威尔的浸信会牧师，在十九世纪时到处讲一个故事，人们花钱去听，因为那时候没有电视，所以人们付费去听讲座。

他在整个美国，整个美洲，到处讲这个故事，并因此赚了数百万美元。

然后他用这笔钱，在费城创办了我们这里一所伟大的大学，天普大学。

所以，我要把这个故事讲给你听，然后我们再回过头来，把它和这门课程关于成功的材料联系起来。

故事大概是这样的。

从前有个农夫名叫阿里·哈菲德，他住在中东，经营着自己的小农场，有家庭，勤劳肯干，虽然勉强维持生计，但也过得下去。

有一天，一位来自远东的佛教僧侣在朝圣途中路过此地，问他能否在阿里·哈菲德家借住几天，他同意了。

一天晚上吃饭时，这位佛教僧侣开始谈论他的旅程，他说世界上有些地方可以找到钻石。

那些钻石非常了不起，非常非常值钱。

阿里·哈菲德以前从未听说过钻石，于是他请僧侣再多讲讲钻石的事。

佛教僧侣描述了钻石的奇妙特性，它们闪闪发光，备受人们喜爱，能制成精美的珠宝，价格昂贵。

于是，阿里·哈菲德开始渴望能找到一些这样的钻石。

他问佛教僧侣在哪里可以找到钻石。

佛教僧侣若有所思地说，嗯，你总是能辨认出它们在哪里。

有钻石地区的山脉，你知道，会呈现出某种特定的山峰形状。

然后山脚下会有一条河流过。

河水流经之处会有一些银色的沙地。

如果你看向这清澈的河水，就能在水下看到钻石。

然后，你知道，在这些具有这种特征的地方，钻石是取之不尽的。

所以阿里·哈菲德，你知道，这下是彻底被说服了。

于是他决定要去寻找，出发去为自己找些钻石，变得富有。

于是他离开了家人。

他打包好所有长途旅行的物资。

然后就出发去寻找那个能发现钻石的地方了。

他到处寻找。

他找遍高地，找遍低谷，最终却成了一个落魄的人。

他寻找了一辈子。

从未找到那个有钻石的地方。

他历经千辛万苦。

最后，在绝望中，他投身大海，结束了自己的生命。

与此同时，回到农场，有人买下了阿里·哈菲德的农场并接手经营。

一天，新主人来到了屋后的地里。

当然，他们抬眼望向就在农场后面的群山。

群山以一种特定的方式矗立着。

有一条河在农场后面的区域流淌，流经那片山区。

河床上有些地方是银色的沙地。

这位新主人注意到水下有一点微弱的闪光，便伸手下去捡了起来，是一颗钻石。

然后又伸手下去捡起另一颗，又是一颗钻石。

结果发现，阿里·哈菲德整个农场后面那四十英亩的土地，竟然是一个巨大的钻石矿，成为了当时世界上已知的最大钻石矿。

故事讲到这里，康威尔牧师就会说，所以这个故事的教训是，不要到遥远的异乡去寻找财富和繁荣。

它就在你自己的后院里。

如果你住在费城，就在费城寻找你能做的一切。

如果你住在纽约，你就会说，在纽约寻找你能做的一切，在你所在的地方建立你的财富。

在我们的课程中，我们想说的是，你自己就是你的后院，你的任务就是审视自己的能力、你的兴趣，去发现你自身拥有的钻石，以此为基础，你将如何获得满足感、幸福感，以及实现任何你认为值得拥有的成就。

因此，我们在课程中定位了四种不同的钻石，这将是我们下一节要讨论的主题。
